newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Prisoners on hunger strike in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Prisoners on hunger strike in South Korea.

text.p: Prisoners at a South Korean jail have gone on hunger strike in protest against last week's arrests of pro-North Korean students, domestic Yonhap news agency said on Wednesday.

Yonhap quoted officials at the prison in the southern city of Kwangju as saying about 20 prisoners had gone on hunger strike because of the arrests on November 13 of 24 of students forming a pro-North Korean "National Liberation Army".
The students were charged under the National Security law that guards against subversion from communist North Korea.
An official at the prison, speaking by telephone, said he could not comment on the Yonhap report.
"I have nothing to tell you. The only thing I can tell you is we have notified authorities of the incident," he said.
Yonhap said the prisoners, most of them serving sentences for their involvement in pro-North Korean activities, argued the reason for the arrests had been "fabricated" by authorities.

On November 13, prosecutors alleged the "National Liberation Army" was a branch of a radical student council, the Hanchongryon, that led violent protests in support of Korean unification at Seoul's Yonsei University in August.

A total of 444 students have gone on trial for their roles in the demonstrations in which one policeman died and hundreds of officers and students were injured. So far, 225 have been sentenced to jail terms or given suspended sentences.
A demilitarized zone, the world's last cold war frontier, sealed the division of the Korean peninsula between north and south after the 1950-53 Korean War.
